risks: The engineer meets 920 W1-02 cases and 91 W2-50 cases going red that no designer has rewritten yet. The four test-designer listing cases depend on reading "aimed listing … as in 3" as applying to the test designer (TD-3). Root-search refusal cases in my suite pass today for DEC-557's reason, so on those cases a pass alone proves nothing until the implementation lands.
lessons: Find earlier cases by running the suite with a plugin that logs the guard's refusal reason per test, not by grep. Split W1-02 by file to stay under 10 minutes per command. Use the Edit tool, never here-documents or `$VAR` write targets. W1-02's fixture holds an engineer acceptance folder (`tests/acceptance/W1-90/`) and a link `src/gov/guard/acceptance_link`, so "for every role" cases need a separate expectation for the engineer under (c).
proposed_decisions: **P-W2-58-TD-1** — Question: how do the 920 W1-02 cases and 91 W2-50 cases reach Policy 2? Why now: they go red the moment W2-58's guard lands. Options: (a) a fresh designer session in this ticket rewrites them in place from `EARLIER_CASES.md`, after TD-2 is decided (about 3–5 h); (b) the orchestrator or owner marks W1-02's protected-read batches as superseded, and a designer cuts each function down to a few allowed forms per family; (c) carry them as accepted reds (fails the "every suite green" bar). Impact: blocks W2-58's close. Reversible: yes. **Recommendation (a), confidence medium.** **P-W2-58-TD-2** — Readings no source states: (i) a second name (`mv`, `cp -l`, `ln`) of the settings file or its folder: once reads are open, is it allowed, or is a hard link a write alias that "no write rule widens" must refuse? Recommendation: refuse a hard link or move of a file the role may not write, as a write; allow a symbolic link or copy into a writable place. Confidence medium. (ii) Copies of the two files elsewhere, and `~/.claude/settings.json`: open (DEC-820 replaces "nobody reads anything under `~/.claude/`"). Confidence medium-high. (iii) DEC-570 bounded-time refusals: keep a refusal where the new rules cannot decide in time (DEC-580). Confidence low-medium. (iv) Is an engineer subagent of the orchestrator an engineer under (c), and on whose ticket? No recommendation. (v) DEC-562's NUL-byte refusal stays, as input hygiene, not a read restriction (untouched). Confidence medium. **P-W2-58-TD-3** — Should the test designer's aimed listings (Glob, `ls`, `find` of a folder holding changed files) be refused? Its names are open through `git diff --name-only`. Options: (a) keep them refused, as the brief and my 4 cases say; (b) allow them, and I flip those 4 cases. Recommendation (a); low cost either way; confidence medium.
unresolved: The 920 + 91 earlier cases (TD-1); TD-2 (i)–(v); the subagent case `test_a_search_tool_call_from_the_root_is_refused_for_a_role_subagent_too` left as it was. Refusals I met: **1 guard read refusal (DEC-849)**, a `gov retrieve` whose question text named the two files. Also refused: one Bash write with a `$VAR` target and two shell commands refused as unreadable (DEC-409: a here-document, and a script containing backticks). None was refused twice for the same call. `gov retrieve` was used twice for the decisions: once refused (above), once `STORE_MISSING` (this worktree has no store, and loading one would write outside `.gov-runtime/scratch/`), so I read the register directly.
